title: Route Four Mornings, Including a Crash
scenario: It is 6:38 AM. Four mornings to route under policy 1.1.0 (escalate at 14 or more). One of them is a price CRASH - a big move DOWN. Markets falling need approval as much as markets spiking, and this is where hand-rolled branches usually get it wrong.
input:
Escalation rule (Threshold Policy v1.1.0): a day-over-day move of 14 percent OR MORE - in either direction - requires manager approval. Escalated mornings route to approval-route; all others to routine-update-path.

Four mornings (biggest day-over-day move that day):
day-1 (today): +15.9 percent (ERCOT)
day-2: -14.0 percent (SPP crashed)
day-3: +13.9 percent (ERCOT)
day-4: -5.8 percent (WAUE)
instructions: Apply the rule to the SIZE of each move: -14.0 is a 14-point move.
Watch both traps: the negative boundary case AND the just-under case.
Record the signed move in biggestMovePct but classify on magnitude.
Return a JSON array with one object per day, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Route four days: a move of 14 percent or more IN EITHER DIRECTION escalates to approval-route; others go to routine-update-path. Days: +15.9, -14.0, +13.9, -5.8. Keep the signed value in biggestMovePct but classify on absolute size. Return a JSON array of { day, biggestMovePct, escalationRequired, route }.
successMessage: Four mornings routed - including the crash that naive branches wave through.

intro.heading: Before you build: the absolute-value bug

sections.title: The most common branch bug in finance automation
sections.body: Someone writes 'if move >= 14 escalate' and ships it. Spikes escalate; crashes sail through, because -14 is not greater than 14. The rule was always about magnitude; the code quietly wasn't. Day-2 exists to make you feel this bug.

sections.title: Two boundaries at once
sections.body: Day-2 is negative AND exactly at the threshold: abs(-14.0) = 14.0, and the rule says OR MORE. Day-3 sits at 13.9 - just under. Passing both proves the branch, not luck.

sections.title: Sign in the record, magnitude in the rule
sections.body: The log keeps -14.0 because direction matters to readers (a crash reads differently than a spike). The classification uses 14.0 because the rule is about size. One value, two uses.

fieldGuide.hint: Judge the size of the move, not its sign.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd apply the rule - auto-approve if within tolerance, otherwise send to a person - so obvious cases don't wait on a human.

tools.powerAutomate: 'Condition' -> either auto-complete or 'Start and wait for an approval'
tools.zapier: 'Filter'/'Paths' that auto-pass clean cases and route the rest

takeaway.heading: The crash got caught
points: You routed a negative boundary case correctly - the exact spot where 'if move >= threshold' silently fails in production.
You held both boundary disciplines at once: -14.0 escalates (or-more on magnitude), +13.9 does not (just under).
The log keeps signed values so readers see crash vs spike, while the rule reads magnitude - one number serving two masters, explicitly.
Today (day-1) escalates again - and the approval handoff ahead has a complication waiting.
The workflow can now route on the size of a move regardless of its direction.
